configurations.// why-host: --host is REQUIRED, not a convenience. Without it astro dev binds IPv6 loopback ONLY ([::1]:4321) - measured 28 Jul 2026: curl to 127.0.0.1:4321 got no listener at all while [::1]:4321 returned 200. Windows resolves localhost to 127.0.0.1 first in most browsers, so the server looks dead from a browser while curl and any IPv6-first client say it is fine. With --host it binds 0.0.0.0 and [::] and both answer.
configurations.name: astro-dev

configurations.// why: The Astro CLI is a singleton daemon: `npm run dev` from a worktree ignores --port and reuses the main checkout's :4321, so it serves the WRONG code and a verification against it is worse than none. Serving the built dist/ on its own port is how a worktree gets honest eyes on its own changes. Run `npm run build` first.
configurations.name: dist-static

configurations.// why: Same job as dist-static, but WITHOUT the pinned port, because the pin is a trap when two sessions are open. `dist-static` hardcodes -l 4325, so a second session cannot start one: the port is taken, and the server already there is serving a DIFFERENT checkout's dist. Measured 1 Aug 2026 - a freshly built /_astro/ModuleRows.<hash>.css returned 404 from :4325 while the page there still linked the old hash, so a verification against it would have measured another branch's CSS and called it this one's. `serve` reads the PORT env var, which autoPort supplies, so this entry gets a free port and serves THIS working tree. Run `npm run build` first.
configurations.name: dist-static-auto
